scope: Fees an Upwork freelancer pays: the Freelancer Service Fee on earnings and the fee for withdrawing them. Client-side fees, Connects, PayPal and Payoneer withdrawal fees and sales tax on fees are out of scope.
structure: Upwork charges freelancers a Freelancer Service Fee on earnings. The rate ranges from 0% to 15% per contract, is shown on the offer or proposal before you accept, and is fixed once the contract begins. Upwork Payroll and Any Hire contracts pay no service fee; Direct Contracts pay a reduced fee. Withdrawals cost nothing to a U.S. bank for freelancers with a US tax address, $2.99 to a U.S. bank for freelancers with an international tax address (from September 1, 2026), $0.99 to a local bank outside the US, $50.00 by U.S. dollar wire and $2.00 by Instant Pay.
summary: Upwork takes a Freelancer Service Fee of 0% to 15% of your earnings, set per contract and shown before you accept. Withdrawing to a U.S. bank is free for US-based freelancers; other methods cost $0.99 to $50.00 per withdrawal.

quotes: It’s the fee you pay on your Upwork earnings. The fee ranges from 0% to 15% per contract, and helps us provide you with payment protection, fraud prevention, dispute resolution, and all the tools that help you run your business more smoothly.
Once your contract begins, the fee is fixed and won’t change.
You’ll see the fee percentage when a client sends you an offer, or you are submitting a proposal, so you always know the exact fee that applies beforehand.
The 10% fee is $26.664 USD or $26.66 USD when rounded down to nearest cent
Your net earnings are $239.98 USD ($0.02 less than estimated, 12 x $20 = $240 USD)
The 10% fee is $33.336 USD or $33.34 USD when rounded up to nearest cent
Your net earnings are $300.02 USD ($0.02 more than estimated, 12 x $25 USD = $300 USD)
No, we are not offering any regular discounts.
Upwork Payroll: Freelancers participating in the Upwork Payroll service are paid through a third-party staffing firm and are therefore excluded from paying an Upwork Freelancer Service Fee.
Any Hire: If you work for a client on an Any Hire contract, you will not pay a Freelancer Service Fee.
Direct Contracts: If you have created a Direct Contracts contract with a client you brought to Upwork, you’ll pay a reduced Freelancer Service Fee.

Free for Freelancers with US Tax Address
2.99 for Freelancers with International Tax Address (Effective September 1st, 2026)
Direct to Local Bank (outside of U.S.) — $0.99 USD per transfer
U.S. Dollar Wire Transfer — $50.00 USD per transfer
Instant Pay for U.S. Freelancers — $2.00 USD per transfer
The cost per withdrawal direct to your local bank is $0.99 USD (plus incoming fees at some banks).
Direct to U.S. Bank withdrawals are free for freelancers with a United States tax address.
excluded: Client-side fees: the client marketplace fee and the contract initiation fee.
Connects, the credits freelancers spend to send proposals.
PayPal and Payoneer withdrawals, whose fees Upwork says vary by location.
Sales tax on service fees where it applies.
The reduced Direct Contracts fee and Enterprise rates, which Upwork does not state as a number on the loaded pages.
notes: Upwork does not publish how it sets each contract's rate within 0% to 15%; it shows the rate before you accept. Enter that rate in the calculator.
Upwork's two worked examples round to the nearest cent: $26.664 becomes $26.66 and $33.336 becomes $33.34. The calculator reproduces both.
Upwork says it is 'not offering any regular discounts' on the service fee.
The withdrawal fee is charged per withdrawal, not per contract. The calculator applies it as if these earnings were withdrawn on their own.
